simple: The Curve Editor is a special view inside the Animation Editor that shows your animation as colored lines on a graph. Each line shows how one value, like a rotation around X, Y, or Z, changes over time. By bending these lines you control exactly how smooth, sharp, or bouncy the motion feels. It is a more advanced tool for when you want your animations to look extra polished.
analogy: It is like a speed graph for a roller coaster ride: a steep part of the line means fast change, a flat part means the motion is barely changing at that moment.
keyPoints: Switch to it by clicking the Curve Editor icon in the top-left of the timeline. Your `KeyframeSequence` clip converts to a `CurveAnimation` clip.
Before switching, pick your Default Rotation Type (Euler Angles or Quaternions) in the settings icon menu. Converting quaternions to Euler angles cannot be undone.
The position ruler on the left and rotation ruler on the right show values for your selected tracks.
Tangents are handles on the curve. Drag them to change how motion flows into and out of a keyframe; right-click and choose Set Tangent To Zero to reset one.
Interpolation modes are Linear (steady, the default), Constant (snaps), and Cubic (eases, and the only mode with tangents).
Bounce and Elastic are not normal modes here. Select two or more keyframes, right-click, and use Generate Curve to fake them.
Euler angles order (like XYZ or ZYX) sets which axis turns first. Changing it on an existing Euler track can change how the animation looks.

terms.curve: A line on the graph showing how one value changes over time.
terms.dope sheet: The normal Animation Editor timeline view that shows keyframes as dots on rows, without the curves.
terms.Euler angles: Rotation written as three angles: how much to turn around X, around Y, and around Z, like 0, 45, 0 for a 45 degree turn left.
terms.quaternion: A different math way to store rotation that always takes the shortest path and avoids certain glitches. Harder to read, but steady.
terms.gimbal lock: A glitch with Euler angles where two axes line up and you lose one direction of turning, which can make motion twist oddly.
terms.interpolation: Filling in the values between two keyframes so the rig moves smoothly instead of jumping.
terms.tangent: A handle on a keyframe that bends the curve. Pulling it changes how fast the motion starts or ends around that keyframe.
terms.Cubic: An interpolation mode that eases in and out smoothly, like a car speeding up and slowing down gently.
terms.Euler angles order: Which axis rotation is applied first. XYZ means the rig turns on Z first, then Y, then X.
terms.axis: One of the three directions: X (side to side), Y (up and down), Z (forward and back).

watchOut: Opening the Curve Editor without checking the rotation type. Choose Quaternions first if you want the animation to stay exactly the same, since Euler conversion is permanent.
Trying to drag tangents on a Linear or Constant keyframe. Only Cubic keyframes have tangents.
Looking for Bounce and Elastic in the interpolation menu. Use Generate Curve instead.
Changing the Euler angles order on finished Euler tracks. It can change the motion, so pick the order early.
